chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: After-hours jamming and cutting sessions
summary: Other musicians came to hear the Blue Devils jam all night, which made their name; Lester Young, Charlie Parker and Ben Webster jammed in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What confuses me a little bit is, if you had, and you undoubtedly did have this reputation for playing great solos and for playing very good Jazz music... But at the same time, if you were playing all this sweet stuff all the time, how could anybody know that you could do all this? Where did the other guys get to hear you play?
Oh, they'd come around when we'd play some of these colored places. They'd be off; they'd come around and listen to us. Yeah.
Was it a jamming band? I mean, when you'd go to a town to do a gig, would you all go on somewhere afterwards, to after-hours places?
Yeah. We did it all the time. Heh-heh...
But some bands didn't like to do that.
Yeah. That's why they got known so. All the other bands knew if their cats came around there, that's where you'd learn something. Go out and blow all night long. All night!
Did you used to like to do that?

Yeah, I did that. But I got ..(?)... and I said "Oh, I ain't dealing with this ...(?)..." I cut it out. I'll go down and listen at the (?) and you all quit that staying up all night, jammin' and goin' on. But Lester Young, Charlie Parker and all of them would go down there, and Ben Webster would go ...(?)... and blow all night long in Kansas City.
